name: adhd
what_it_does: Reshapes every reply for the rest of the session: the next action first, numbered steps, your position restated each turn, and tangents left out.
what_you_get: Answers in a fixed shape, with the next concrete step at the top and a time estimate on it, until you say to stop.

name: capability-index
what_it_does: Keeps a list of skills that exist on your computer but are not loaded in the session you are in, and says where each one lives.
what_you_say: is there a skill for this that isn't loaded?
what_you_get: The name of what covers your request, where it lives, and an offer to install it or switch it on.
on_your_computer: Reads the file that records which packs you have installed and lists the folders in your library. It installs or switches on a pack only after you say yes.

name: fable-project-review
what_it_does: Reviews a project you already built, ranks what is wrong by severity, and writes a plan a later session can carry out without your help.
what_you_say: review this project and tell me what you'd improve
what_you_get: A review by dimension, then a dated plan file with exact file paths, the wanted end state and a check for each item.
on_your_computer: Reads through the project you name, runs `git log` to see recent changes, and writes one or two dated markdown files into that project folder.

name: folder-to-repo
what_it_does: Turns a folder with no history into a new private GitHub repository, scanning it for secrets before the first commit.
what_you_get: A private repository holding your files, a README and a `.gitignore`, and a list of anything the scan left out.
on_your_computer: Reads every text file in the folder, adds a README and `.gitignore`, creates a git repository with a first commit, deletes a file named `START_HERE.md`, then creates a private GitHub repository and uploads the folder.

name: graham-voice
what_it_does: Drafts emails, messages and notes in one named person's writing voice, down to his phrasing and sign-offs.
what_you_say: reply to this in my voice
what_you_get: A draft for you to edit. It never sends anything.

name: humanizer
what_it_does: Rewrites text that sounds like a chatbot so it reads like a person, keeping every fact, and naming the patterns it removed.
what_you_say: make this sound less like AI wrote it
what_you_get: The rewrite, plus a short list of what changed and of any chatbot patterns still left in it.
on_your_computer: Reads the one file you name and can overwrite it, but only after showing you the rewrite and getting a yes in that conversation.

name: repo-handoff
what_it_does: Cuts a copy of a project you can give to another person, with your personal and copyrighted material removed and proven gone.
what_you_say: make a copy of this project I can hand to a friend
what_you_get: A private repository for the recipient, the list of what was left out and why, and a walkthrough that was run before handover.
on_your_computer: Searches your repository and its whole history for the details you list, builds a cleaned copy in a scratch folder, runs a secret scanner over it, then creates a private GitHub repository and uploads that copy.

name: schedule-harness
what_it_does: Writes the instruction file for running one phase of a long project on a schedule, with written limits on what an unwatched run may do.
what_you_say: set this phase up to run every Sunday
what_you_get: One small instruction file, a check that it is complete, and the values you paste in to register the job.
on_your_computer: Writes two small text files, a short input file and then the file describing an unattended job, and checks the second one. You register the job yourself.

name: scrollback
what_it_does: Builds pages, dashboards, documents and slides in one fixed monospace style, with a set list of colours and components.
what_you_say: build this page in the Scrollback style
what_you_get: The page or stylesheet you asked for, and on request a table of how readable each colour pairing is.
on_your_computer: Writes the web page you asked for and can run a small colour check. The pages it makes fetch a font from Google when someone opens them.

name: skill-discovery
what_it_does: Reads your past Claude conversations for jobs you set up from scratch again and again, and ranks them as candidates for new skills.
what_you_say: what am I doing repeatedly that should be a skill?
what_you_get: A ranked list of candidates, each with the phrases that would trigger it and the conversations that are the evidence.
on_your_computer: Reads your past Claude conversations, runs several helper agents over them, and offers to save one list of suggestions.

name: source-intake
what_it_does: Judges an incoming repository or article against what you already have installed, then applies the decisions you agree to.
what_you_get: A review written without your own setup in view, a comparison against what you already have, and a table of decisions.
on_your_computer: Downloads the repository or article you point at, runs several separate Claude reviews of it, then edits and commits files in your skill library.

name: toolkit-review
what_it_does: Judges the skills, agents and hooks you already have, one slot at a time, on their own or against a repository you are considering.
what_you_say: review my skills and tell me which ones earn their place
what_you_get: A scored ledger per slot, two independent judgments each way round, a decisions table, and changes that wait for your approval.
on_your_computer: Copies your installed skills and any downloaded repositories into a working folder, runs many separate Claude sessions and, at the largest size, throwaway containers over them, writes a folder of report files, and can end by committing changes to your skill library.

name: x-read
what_it_does: Fetches the full text of a post, a long article or a whole thread on X, or runs a search there, and hands it back as plain text.
what_you_say: read this X thread for me
what_you_get: The full text as markdown or as structured data, without the preview cut-off you get elsewhere.
on_your_computer: Runs a Node program that talks to X as you, using two session cookies you stored once yourself, downloads the posts you name, and keeps one small cache file in `~/.config/bird`.
